column1: *** ESTADO CIVIL: DIVORCIADO ***
column2: the box is ticked for divorced, not single and not widowed — sixty-two years after the wedding of 1939 and sixty-five after she left Mozambique. The Portuguese state recorded her to the end as a divorcée, which is what averbamento 2 of her birth entry made her in December 1945.

column2: freguesia de Nossa Senhora da Conceição, concelho de Lourenço Marques — Moçambique. Identical to the assento.

column1: *** RESIDÊNCIA HABITUAL: RUA NOVA DAS MARINHAS 82, GULPILHARES, VILA NOVA DE GAIA, DISTRITO DO PORTO, PORTUGAL ***
column2: she died where she lived. THIS ARCHIVE HAD NO PORTUGUESE ADDRESS FOR HER AT ALL and no indication she had returned to Portugal.

column1: *** DIED AT HOME — "num domicílio" — AT 04:30 ***
column2: local do óbito is ticked for a private dwelling rather than a hospital or clinic.

column1: the date is March 2010 and the day is NOT legible enough to publish
column2: the boxed digits read as 16 or 17 and this archive will not choose between them by eye. WHAT BOUNDS IT: the certifying physician dated his signature 16/03/2010, and the whole bundle was faxed the same day at 14:38. So the death is on or immediately before 16 March 2010, and she was 88.

column1: what would settle the day
column2: the assento de óbito at the Conservatória do Registo Civil for Vila Nova de Gaia, or the averbamento of death that should now sit on the birth entry transcribed above.

column1: causa da morte, Parte I (a)
column2: FALÊNCIA CARDIO-RESPIRATÓRIA — cardio-respiratory failure. Approximate interval between onset and death: more than one year.

column1: causa da morte, Parte II
column2: *** DEMÊNCIA *** — dementia, also more than a year, recorded as a contributing condition rather than the direct cause.

column1: tipo de óbito
column2: NATURAL. The cause was given on clinical grounds, with no autopsy, and the certificate records that a physician had attended her in the seven days before she died.

column1: *** JACINTO DE ARAÚJO FERNANDES DE OLIVEIRA — IVONE'S PARTNER UNTIL HER DEATH ***
column2: faxed with this certificate on 16 March 2010 at 14:38 is a DECLARAÇÃO signed at SANTA MARINHA, a parish of Vila Nova de Gaia, in which he declares that he is giving lodging to "o Sr. DERIKE" on his journey to Portugal — an accommodation letter of the kind a consulate asks for. HE WAS NOT A HOUSEHOLDER WITH A SPARE ROOM. He was her partner, confirmed by the family on 27 September 2026.

column1: *** WHICH SON TRAVELLED IS NOT SETTLED, AND THE DOCUMENT AND THE FAMILY DISAGREE ***
column2: the declaration names "o Sr. DERIKE", which is how a Portuguese hand writes DERRICK down from speech. THE FAMILY'S RECOLLECTION IS THAT IT WAS HENRIQUE — known in the family as ERIC — who stayed with Jacinto through his mother's death, and that HENRIQUE AFTERWARDS PASSED THESE DOCUMENTS TO DERRICK, which is how they reach this archive at all. A clerk does not turn Henrique into Derike; a clerk does turn Derrick into it. Both brothers were travelling from southern Africa and both would have needed such a letter, and both may have gone. LEFT UNRESOLVED RATHER THAN TIDIED.

column1: *** AND IF IT WAS HENRIQUE, THE ARCHIVE'S ACCOUNT OF HIM IS INCOMPLETE ***
column2: the Ivone page has him left behind in Mozambique, reaching Johannesburg twenty-one years later, and says nothing of him after 1962. A HENRIQUE AT VILA NOVA DE GAIA IN 2010, IN HIS MOTHER'S PARTNER'S HOUSE, MEANS WHATEVER PASSED BETWEEN THE SON SHE LEFT AND THE MOTHER WHO LEFT HIM DID NOT END IN 1941. And the papers reached Derrick through his half-brother, so the two were in contact late in life. ERIC is also a name variant this archive did not hold.

column1: what that adds, and it is a relationship this archive had no idea existed
column2: IVONE HAD A PARTNER IN PORTUGAL AT THE END OF HER LIFE. The archive's account of her ran out in South Africa in the 1950s and resumed only at "she died and was buried at Porto". She was married four times between 1939 and 1953 — Pinto da Rocha, de Witt, Luwinski, Salkow — and the Portuguese state recorded her to the end as DIVORCIADO, so this last attachment was not a marriage. His own declaration gives his status as DIVORCIADO too.

column1: the two addresses are not the same, and that is worth noticing rather than smoothing over
column2: SHE DIED AT RUA NOVA DAS MARINHAS 82, GULPILHARES. HIS DECLARATION GIVES HIS OWN ADDRESS AT PRACETA FERNÃO DE MAGALHÃES 101, SANTA MARINHA. Both are parishes of VILA NOVA DE GAIA, about three kilometres apart. Whether they kept separate homes, or whether the declaration simply cites his registered address, is not something this document decides.

column1: *** AND HE IS THE ONLY LIVING LINK THIS ARCHIVE EVER HAD TO HER PORTUGUESE YEARS, NOW GONE ***
column2: both he and Ivone are deceased. A partner is the person who would have known where she lived between 1953 and 2010, whether she ever saw Henrique again, and which of her papers survive. THE QUESTION TO PUT TO DERRICK IS WHETHER JACINTO HAD CHILDREN OR SIBLINGS, because they would have known her too.

column1: what is not published, and it is a judgement rather than a rule
column2: the declaration carries his BILHETE DE IDENTIDADE NUMBER and his CONTRIBUINTE (taxpayer) NUMBER. Both are withheld. THE LIVING-PEOPLE RULE NO LONGER APPLIES — he is dead and the family has said so — but a national identity number and a tax number carry no genealogical information whatever: they locate a man in a state's filing system, not in a family. They are in the private notes, where they can be quoted at a Portuguese archive if one ever asks for them.
